+def _merge_update(ids, pair, idx, stats):
+    """
+    Same result as merge(ids, pair, idx), and additionally updates the pair
+    counts in stats (as from get_stats(ids)) to those of the merged list:
+    only pairs touching a merged occurrence change. Zero counts are removed.
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    k = ids.count(p0)
+    if not k:
+        return list(ids)
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    newids = []
+    extend = newids.extend
+    append = newids.append
+    index = ids.index
+    last = len(ids) - 1
+    same = p0 == p1
+    touched = []
+    tappend = touched.append
+    prev_end = -1 # old position right after the previous merged occurrence
+    i = 0
+    while k:
+        j = index(p0, i)
+        k -= 1
+        if j < last and ids[j+1] == p1:
+            extend(ids[i:j])
+            append(idx)
+            stats[pair] -= 1
+            if j:
+                if prev_end == j:
+                    # left neighbour is the previous merged token; the old pair
+                    # (p1, p0) was already removed as its right pair
+                    p = (idx, idx)
+                else:
+                    a = ids[j-1]
+                    p = (a, p0)
+                    stats[p] -= 1
+                    tappend(p)
+                    p = (a, idx)
+                stats[p] = stats_get(p, 0) + 1
+            if j + 2 <= last:
+                b = ids[j+2]
+                p = (p1, b)

+                    # right neighbour stays (otherwise counted as the next left pair)

actions.reason: BasicTokenizer.train recounted all pairs over the whole id list (get_stats) on every merge step. Now pair counts are computed once and updated incrementally inside a merge variant (_merge_update) that only touches the pairs adjacent to each merged occurrence (with dedup for back-to-back occurrences and p0==p1), deleting zero counts so the stats equal a fresh get_stats as a multiset. Tie-breaking is preserved: when several pairs share the max count, the pair whose first occurrence in ids is earliest (what max() over a fresh dict returns) is found with a C-level compress scan. Equivalence harness identical; train_ir 0.79x.
